text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The leu currency seems to have reached a balanced rate of around 4,300 to the dollar on the interbank market.
- The International Monetary Fund might resume credits to Romania in January.
- Azomures SA fertiliser maker continues to be the most actively traded stock on the Bucharest bourse.
- The new government said the price of petrol would be "revised periodically" and energy prices would be increased gradually before liberalisation in 1998.
AZI
- Shipping company Romline sold a 4,500 dwt ship to British company Sally Line.
ZIUA
- The National Oil Company proposed a rise in the price of petrol to 1,500 lei per litre.
- IMF experts will resume talks with Romania on new credits in January.
- The Trade Ministry approved exports of 500,000 tonnes of maize in the first half of 1997.
LIBERTATEA
- Shareholders' certificates under the mass selloff scheme were distributed to 76 percent of the 15 million Romanian who subscribed for company shares in exchange for coupons.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Trade unions in the electricity sector demand a 40 percent rise in electricity prices, saying the sector had losses this year.
General
All newspapers report on the debate and vote in parliament which adopted the cabinet list and economic programme of Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
ADEVARUL

- The conclusion of the Romanian-Hungarian friendship treaty, the presence of the Hungarian Democratic Union in government and centrist victory in last month's election improve Romania's chances of joining European and Euro-Atlantic structures, says an editorial.
LIBERTATEA
- Pope John Paul accepted an invitation to visit Romania, but no date has been set yet.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The new government will include a special anti-corruption department under direct control of the prime minister.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The number of cars in Bucharest doubled to 500,000 over the past seven years, the traffic police chief says in an interview. ($=3,687 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
